sources.title: Bharati Pal: Lord Jagannath in Suryavamsi Inscriptions, Orissa Review 2007, pp. 112-114
sources.note: Original government journal article, p. 112 read through indexed original; direct PDF timed out. Reproducible title query plus Pundarika. Same text appears in complete June-July issue; treated as one work. Bounded salt/cowry tax remission and sari gift; no claim that every household followed temple practice.

sources.title: R. Subrahmanyam: The Suryavamsi Gajapatis of Orissa, 1957, chapters 3 and 7
sources.note: Original scholarly monograph read through OCR mirror. Printed pp. 145-146: Simhachalam teaching endowment, 1291; p. 154: Laksanadarsa grammar through Pandava story. Chapter 3, printed pp. 32-34, separately read at /d/doc1602975.html for accession 1435 and initial opposition. Both chapters counted as one work. No legendary childhood adopted.

sources.title: P. Srinivasachar and accompanying epigraphic discussion: Warangal inscription of Ambira-deva
sources.note: Institutional epigraphic compilation, printed pp. 54-55, PDF indices 53-55. Direct text and indexed original checked. Telugu prose inscription at Warangal gateway commemorates Ambira-deva, son of Kapilendra, capturing fort; editor converts date to 2 February 1460. Vadda-varamu explicitly glossed Saturday, including bilingual parallels. Direction of gateway placement differs between reports, so omitted. No unverified Telugu glyph reconstruction.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Sun Temple, Konark
sources.note: Directly read description and Outstanding Universal Value. Thirteenth-century Eastern Ganga monument under Narasimha Deva I, carved chariot wheels and social/musical imagery. Horse counts differ within page, so not quoted. Temple predates imported 1279 start and is labelled inherited context.

sources.title: National Monuments Authority: Barabati Fortress heritage report, archaeological history
sources.note: Directly read 58-page report, chapter 3, PDF indices 10-12. Period II is fifteenth-sixteenth centuries; pillared hall, courtyard, infill finds, painted plaster and Chinese porcelain. Swinging-couple sculpture recovered from moat and attributed stylistically to Gajapati period. Palace storey count and OCR pillar count omitted as inconsistent.

sources.title: Pravakar Sethi: Voices of the people: Social and Domestic life in Medieval Odishan Writings, 2025, pp. 262-268
sources.note: Author-posted original paper read directly; title/author/pages independently indexed by publisher sanskritarticle.com, volume 63. Bounded use of p. 264 food and wedding descriptions explicitly as Sethi reading Sarala Dasa, not representative social survey. Paper itself notes textual variation/interpolation, p. 263. Unreliable broad historical framing and plant identification excluded.

sources.title: Bhagaban Panda: Sanskrit poets and scholars flourished during the Suryavamsi Gajapati period, OHRJ XLVII(3)
sources.note: Original government historical research journal, printed p. 70, indexed text read. Reproducible query exact URL plus Kapilendra 1435; confirms Parasurama Vijaya attribution and performance at temple festival before 1458. Uses this bounded literary fact, not the article’s inconsistent ruler-date labels.

sources.title: Jagannath Mohanty: Administration of the Puri Temple Through Ages, Orissa Review June 2006, pp. 103-105
sources.note: Directly read p. 103: Mukunda death and Afghan conquest in 1568, smaller Khurda kingdom under Ramachandra of Bhoi line, restoration at Puri and continuing temple superintendence. Later colonial chronology not used.

sources.title: Puri district: History, administrative units

proposedOverrides.name: Orissa: Ganga, Gajapati and successor rule
proposedOverrides.summary: Odisha’s later Ganga and Gajapati kingdoms, with expanding power, temple institutions and regional continuity.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact indexed historical-basemaps record only; no aliases. Earlier orissa (1000-1100) is a different imported phase; western-gangas belongs to southern India and is not Eastern Ganga Odisha.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Seven decoded HB polygons, 1279-1650. Maximum eastern bound about 85.38 E excludes Cuttack (85.86), Puri (85.83) and Konark (86.09). Public overview explicitly warns that important centres are omitted. Polygon is not corrected by this narrative.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Imported 1279-1650 spans multiple governments, not a single dynasty. Eastern Ganga to 1435; Gajapati and later successor rulers to conquest in 1568; Afghan and Mughal phases. Konark explicitly predates map start. No exact end date for Prataparudra adopted because consulted publications differ.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Contemporary 1460 Telugu Warangal inscription of Ambira/Hamvira, son of Kapilendra. Quoted Vadda-varamu is the published Roman transliteration, explicitly translated Saturday in the epigraphic source. No unverified original Telugu glyph reconstruction, modern Odia substitute or claim that the text represents every language in the realm.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Sarala-derived food and wedding scenes are attributed literary evidence with manuscript variation, not universal practice. Elite/temple education and temple textile gifts retain institutional scope. Moat sculpture stylistic, displaced context. No medically unsupported remedy or unverified toilet/sanitation system invented.
